card: This pull request calculates headers presync DoS-protection parameters (commitment period and redownload buffer size) at runtime whenever a headers sync starts, removing static precomputed values from chainparams. This eliminates an error-prone release step where maintainers had to predict the release's lifespan using an offline script, while automatically adapting memory bounds as real time progresses. The offline Python tool is deleted and replaced with a closed-form C++ optimization algorithm, backed by unit tests verifying against brute-force search optima and dedicated fuzz targets. No dependencies.
changed_since_previous: Parameters are now recomputed on demand each time a headers sync begins in PeerManagerImpl::TryLowWorkHeadersSync rather than once at node startup, protecting against subsequent clock adjustments, and exhaustive brute-force verification was added to the test suite.
evidence: PR description: 'Less work for maintainers that need to occasionally run the current contrib/devtools/headerssync-params.py script. Less room for mistakes in that process. Automatically adapts based on time (as opposed to needing to predict the lifetime of the software).'

Commit 3ddc510850: 'The old Python code did that, but actually got it (slightly) wrong by missing the fact that attackers are capable of strategically deciding to stop the attack in the middle of a batch (found by darosior).'

Commit 990b3fa6d0: 'A node which starts up with a badly wrong clock and has it corrected before syncing would otherwise use a period sized for a much shorter chain than a peer can then feed it, inflating that bound (by a factor 50 for a clock which starts out before genesis).'
problem: Release maintainers had to manually run an offline Python script during each release and estimate the software's active lifespan to precompute static sync parameters. Hardcoded parameters degrade from optimality as time advances, the old python model had a bug overlooking attackers stopping mid-batch, and sizing parameters statically or once at startup risked skewing memory limits if the system clock was corrected after boot.

risk.why: Incorrectly computed parameters could degrade node DoS resistance against malicious peer headers chains or cause unexpected memory growth during headers sync.

scope_notes: Implements mathematical optimization and continuous relaxation bisection in src/headerssync.cpp alongside extensive brute-force and fuzz testing.
summary: Computes headers presync DoS-protection parameters (commitment period and redownload buffer size) at runtime in C++ whenever a headers sync starts, replacing static precomputed parameters stored in chainparams. Adds a closed-form optimization and bisection search algorithm in headerssync, stores the minimum chainwork height in chainparams consensus parameters, removes the offline python generation script, and adds fuzz and unit test suites.
